gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for Samsung's own keyboards: the Book Cover Keyboard Slim for the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra (EF-DX930) costs $209.99 and has no touchpad, the S10 FE+ Slim (EF-DX620) costs $169.99 and also has no touchpad, and Samsung US now lists the EF-DX930 for the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra too.
standout_why: I read MyNextTablet's 'The 8 Best Tablets With a Keyboard' (cited by ChatGPT, dated 2026-10-19). It already says the S10 FE/FE+ Slim keyboard has no touchpad and doesn't detach, and that on the S11 line a touchpad version is 'currently only available for the S11 Ultra'. It gives no keyboard prices and no total cost with a keyboard. WIRED's page blocked fetching. I couldn't extract text from Samsung's November 2026 MSRP PDF, which ChatGPT also cited, so I can't rule out that it lists keyboard MSRPs. That's why this is a 1, not a 2. What MyNextTablet lacks is the price of each keyboard type and the fact that Samsung US lists the S11 Ultra keyboard for the S12 Ultra.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's own warning to 'compare the total price'. Both Samsung keyboards I could price, $209.99 for the S11 Ultra and $169.99 for the S10 FE+, have no touchpad. A shopper who wants to use DeX like a laptop still needs a touchpad model or a mouse. That costs extra, so the Ultra's 'laptop alternative' price is well above $1,299.99. Samsung US also lists the EF-DX930 for the 'Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra', which suggests a newer Ultra may now be on sale. That could make the S11 Ultra the outdated pick, but I didn't verify it.
